Occurrences.Kwic: 如是則乃可逍遙山谷。放曠郊𮠔。遊逸形儀。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2013.xml). Yongjia Collection of the Chan School (禪宗永嘉集): Yongjia's Collection of the Chan School (禪宗永嘉集), in the letter headed Master Yongjia's Reply to Master Lang and signed by Xuanjue, records Yongjia Xuanjue writing that one may roam through mountains and valleys, range through the outskirts, and let the bearing wander freely. This exact syntax distinguishes motion through terrain from the Mount Xiaoyao place name.

Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin (天隱和尚語錄): The Recorded Sayings of Tianyin Heshang (天隱和尚語錄), spoken by Tianyin Yuanxiu in his own hall address. Tianyin Yuanxiu raises the staff, asks whether it is not roaming at ease and unbound, makes a writing gesture, plants the staff, and leaves the seat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無始刼來，習氣深重，未能頓除，故保任之功，不可或疎。然所謂保任者，非假造作有為之法，不過嘗惺惺地，不為凡心所雜而已。昔天皇悟囑龍潭信曰：任性逍遙，隨緣放曠，但盡凡心，別無聖解。任性逍遙，隨緣放曠二句，切莫錯認，將縱恣放逸，無所忌憚當之。須知所謂逍遙放曠者，乃是於一切妄境，超然不著，如鳥飛空，而毫無所牽繫，如龍出海，而毫無所障礙者也。若聞聲為聲所牽，見色為色所牽，見財為財所礙，見勢為勢所碍，則縛著拘滯甚矣，豈曰放曠逍遙哉？凡若此者，皆為未盡凡心之故也。凡心者何？一有是非之心，凡心也；一有取舍
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1437.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄): The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), in Yongjue Yuanxian's own general address, records his direct definition and its tethering/obstruction contrast. The full exact anchor preserves every image and predicate used in the explanation.

Yongjia Collection of the Chan School (禪宗永嘉集): Yongjia's Collection of the Chan School (禪宗永嘉集), in the letter headed Master Yongjia's Reply to Master Lang and signed by Xuanjue, records Yongjia Xuanjue writing that one may roam through mountains and valleys, range through the outskirts, and let the bearing wander freely. Senses.Explanation: To roam at ease is to move or remain without obstruction in the cited wording. Yongjia Xuanjue pairs it with roaming mountains and valleys; Tianyin Yuanxiu says a staff is ‘at ease and free’; Yongjue Yuanxian contrasts it with being caught by sights, sounds, wealth, or power. These uses concern the action, not either of the two names below.

Senses.Note: The source preserves the title but no personal name.
